root_cause.text: The function `t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler` uses the untrusted, modem-supplied `port_count` field to index into `port_msg->data[]` without verifying that the message buffer is large enough to accommodate `port_count` entries, allowing an attacker-controlled modem to cause a slab-out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that "t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() uses the modem-supplied port_count field as a loop bound over port_msg->data[] without checking that the message buffer contains sufficient data. A modem sending port_count=65535 in a 12-byte buffer triggers a slab-out-of-bounds read of up to 262140 bytes." The patch adds explicit length checks: `if (msg_len < sizeof(*port_msg))` and `if (msg_len < struct_size(port_msg, data, port_count))` before accessing the fields and looping.
